On 10.13.1 with user switching set to username + password, a user logged into the root account from the login screen with no password: 'It's not just a UI bug, it's a full on authentication bypass.'
After turning on Remote Management on a second Mac, a user could log into it via Remote Desktop as root with no password, though it only worked after getting physical access once.

Workaround: once you log in as 'root', change its password to something else and the empty password stops working. Another user suggested setting a root password or disabling root per Apple's support instructions.
Tahoe is a macOS misstep on par with Windows 8 or Vista. The user's feedback to Apple: 'I don't recommend others upgrade. I wish I didn't.'

On Tahoe, windows often refuse to resize, and you end up activating whatever app lies behind the window you're trying to resize, hiding the one you were working with. The user says Mac resizing has long had no visible frame or target zone.
Contrary view: resizing feels easier on Tahoe because the cursor change in the resize area is more dramatic than pre-Tahoe, where the diagonal cursor looked almost the same as the normal arrow.
Tip: Option-double-click any corner to make a window fill the screen without entering full-screen mode. Double-click a side or corner to move it to the screen edge; hold Option to make it symmetric.

Workarounds via third-party tools: one user has long used Moom to move windows without grabbing a particular spot and resize without grabbing a corner ('life changing'). Another recommends Moves for modifier-key drag resizing anywhere in a window.

When Apple's ocsp.apple.com was failing, macOS couldn't complete trustd/syspolicyd checks on opened executables and 'the entire operating system grinds to a halt.' Fix used: add `0.0.0.0 ocsp.apple.com` to /etc/hosts and flush the DNS cache.

MacBook basically unusable until the service recovered: 'Your services hanging should _never_ prevent my device from running things locally. This is seriously making me reconsider my next computer purchase.'
Workaround during the outage: turn off Wi-Fi, reboot, open everything you need, then turn Wi-Fi back on.
Hackintosh and MacBook Air, both on Catalina, froze repeatedly for an hour during the Big Sur release-day outage. Another user was surprised the issue hit their Mojave Mac; Xcode hung during builds.

pbcopy/pbpaste are among a user's most-loved tools: `pbpaste | json_pp | pbcopy` cleans up minified JSON in the clipboard. Several others say they use them all day and miss them on Linux and Raspberry Pi.
networkQuality is a handy built-in replacement for opening Speedtest when checking whether the network is slow.
qlmanage converts SVG to PNG without installing anything extra: `qlmanage -t -s 1000x1000 -o out.png in.svg`.
hidutil remaps keys without extra software, e.g. Caps Lock, or the PC 'Ins' key to something trappable by Keyboard Maestro.

Developing in compiled languages on Catalina, the first execution after each recompile is noticeably delayed. On a spotty tethered connection, another user saw `go build` take up to 30 seconds versus 100ms normally.
On Catalina, switching resolutions or connecting an external screen takes about 10 seconds of flickering and frozen UI, which the user calls worse than both Windows and Linux.

Catalina has many things that synchronously block app launch; if any fail you just get a hung app. The user and a friend trade spindumps trying to find which daemon to kill to get the process responding again.
A Mac user since ~2013 considers moving back to Linux but finds it still horrible outside work for UI/UX. The iOS + macOS ecosystem is still much better than anything else on the market.
